scenes.tts: In 1965, researchers cut the forest on one small watershed at Hubbard Brook, New Hampshire. They used herbicide so nothing grew back. Soon its stream carried far more nitrate than the stream of an uncut watershed nearby. The nitrogen had been there all along. Cutting the trees changed where it went. How would you know where it goes?
scenes.visual: Two watersheds side by side; trees on the right become stumps; its stream arrow thickens while the uncut one stays thin; question mark.
scenes.narration: In 1965, researchers cut the forest on one small watershed at Hubbard Brook, New Hampshire. They used herbicide so nothing grew back. Soon its stream carried far more nitrate than the stream of an uncut watershed nearby. The nitrogen had been there all along. Cutting the trees changed where it went. How would you know where it goes?

scenes.tts: Keep accounts for nitrogen, the way a bank keeps accounts for money. A pool is the amount held in one place at one time, like a balance. A flux is a transfer, like a deposit or a withdrawal. Draw a boundary, and choose an interval, such as a year. Then one rule holds. Change in stock equals inputs minus outputs.
scenes.visual: Boundary draws, pools appear, green deposit and red withdrawal arrows, the rule writes in.
scenes.narration: Keep accounts for nitrogen, the way a bank keeps accounts for money. A pool is the amount held in one place at one time, like a balance. A flux is a transfer, like a deposit or a withdrawal. Draw a boundary, and choose an interval, such as a year. Then one rule holds. Change in stock equals inputs minus outputs.

scenes.tts: Take an invented forest. These numbers are illustrative, in kilograms of nitrogen per hectare per year. Deposition from the air brings in 8. Fixation brings in 6. The stream carries out 3. Denitrification returns 2 to the air as gas. Inputs are 14. Outputs are 5. The forest gains 9, stored in wood and soil.
scenes.visual: Four arrows cross the boundary one by one, tallies add up, plus nine appears and the pools grow.
scenes.narration: Take an invented forest. These numbers are illustrative, in kilograms of nitrogen per hectare per year. Deposition from the air brings in 8. Fixation brings in 6. The stream carries out 3. Denitrification returns 2 to the air as gas. Inputs are 14. Outputs are 5. The forest gains 9, stored in wood and soil.

scenes.tts: Inside the boundary, the soil organic nitrogen pool holds 4,500 kilograms per hectare. Decomposers release 90 of it each year as ammonium. Plants take it up. That flux is about six times the inputs. Yet it never appeared in the sum. An output of one pool is an input of another, so they cancel. Cancelling does not mean turnover is small. Here it is the largest flux.
scenes.visual: Soil to plants flux of 90; bar of 90 against 14; minus 90 plus 90 equals 0.
scenes.narration: Inside the boundary, the soil organic nitrogen pool holds 4,500 kilograms per hectare. Decomposers release 90 of it each year as ammonium. Plants take it up. That flux is about six times the inputs. Yet it never appeared in the sum. An output of one pool is an input of another, so they cancel. Cancelling does not mean turnover is small. Here it is the largest flux.

scenes.tts: Now cut the forest and suppress regrowth. Plant uptake stops. Decomposers keep releasing ammonium, and nitrifiers turn it into nitrate. Soil holds nitrate weakly, so it washes out. Suppose stream export rises to 40, and the other terms stay fixed. Outputs are now 42. The change is 14 minus 42, a loss of 28.
scenes.visual: Plants chip goes grey, uptake arrow is blocked, nitrate dots run to the stream, stream arrow thickens to 40, tally reads minus 28.

scenes.tts: That size is invented. At Hubbard Brook, stream losses of nitrate and of cations such as calcium rose well above those of the uncut reference. The real result shows the direction. The nitrogen was always there. What changed was where it went. Keep the rule. Change in stock equals inputs minus outputs, for a stated boundary and interval.
